run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:33:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error traffic: frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' spans carried ERROR status and its 5xx count rose from 3.3 per 5m at 23:35:40Z to 311.1 per 5m at 23:40:40Z, decaying back to 4.4 by 23:48:40Z (all metric samples 23:13:40Z-23:52:40Z). Traces tie this to the frontend->ad call path: frontend-proxy returned 504 after its 15 s timeout because frontend's /api/data waited 24.6 s on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, whose ad-side server span lasted 22.4 s while ad's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean calls ended DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (grpc 4); later in the same window the frontend got '14 UNAVAILABLE ... ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' from the ad Service and returned 500. The ad Deployment was rollout-restarted at 23:35:00Z with an unchanged pod template (only kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt differs; image, env and resources identical), and the resulting new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was CFS-throttled 95.0-99.9% of periods from 23:35:40Z to 23:42:40Z while pinned at its 50m CPU limit (0.039-0.049 cores), against 6-32% throttling and 0.004-0.011 cores for the old pod - the throttle collapse matches the frontend error window, which ended (0 errors from 23:48:40Z) as throttling fell to ~26%. The only fault-injecting setting switched on in the workload's ConfigMaps is flagd-config's adFailure ('Fail ad service', defaultVariant 'on', state ENABLED); all other flagd fault flags are off. I name that ConfigMap as the root-cause object per the fault-setting rule, with the restart and the frontend-proxy errors as mechanism and consequence, but the conclusion is partial: I did not observe the declared fault behaviour itself (ad GetAds spans returned grpc status 0 with no ad-side ERROR status), I cannot tell when adFailure was switched on, and I cannot tell who or what applied the 23:35:00Z rollout restart (no change-history integration). The CPU-limit/cold-start effect on Deployment ad remains an unrejected alternative mechanism. No error evidence ties the coincident fraud-detection OOMKilled restart to this alert.

claims.text: frontend-proxy has STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for its server span 'ingress' and its client span 'router frontend egress' (service_name=frontend-proxy, exported_job=opentelemetry-demo/frontend-proxy) in the incident window.

frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans (increase over 5m) were 3.33 at 23:35:40Z, 63.33 at 23:36:40Z, 194.44 at 23:38:40Z, peaked at 311.11 at 23:40:40Z, were 31.11 at 23:47:40Z and back to 4.44 by 23:48:40Z, against a total ingress volume of roughly 3,500-3,800 spans per 5m; low-level errors of 1.1-4.4 per 5m existed earlier from 23:17:40Z.

In trace d4057d2e24ea083d01006c39cd8fcd6a the frontend-proxy ingress span returned error=true http.status_code 504 after 15.000 s with a child 'router frontend egress' span of 15.000 s and http.status_code 0, while frontend's 'GET /api/data' lasted 24.594 s, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 24.593 s and ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 22.372 s, whose ad-side flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean spans failed with rpc.grpc.status_code 4.

Ad-side flagd ResolveBoolean client spans were errors with rpc.grpc.status_code 4 (durations 401 ms to 2.50 s) while the matching flagd server spans returned error 'context deadline exceeded' (rpc.grpc.status_code 2) and successful flagd ResolveBoolean server spans served in 49-110 microseconds; ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans in the same sample lasted 4.93-10.50 s with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

At about 23:42:13Z frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080 (2025-12-15T17:53:00.348Z)', frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' returned http.status_code 500, and frontend-proxy ingress returned http.status_code 500 in 2.2-3.6 s.

frontend error spans for 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' and 'GET /api/data' were 0 through 23:35:40Z, 54.44 and 54.44 per 5m at 23:36:40Z, peaked at 304.44 and 297.78 per 5m at 23:39:40Z, were 16.67 at 23:47:40Z and 0 from 23:48:40Z.

The ad pod created at 23:35:00Z, ad-785b4464f5-9bshh, was throttled on 94.97% of CFS periods at 23:35:40Z, 99.85% at 23:39:40Z, 98.87% at 23:42:40Z, 90.21% at 23:43:40Z, 56.72% at 23:44:40Z and 25.75% at 23:45:40Z, while the previous ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was throttled 6.5-31.8% over 23:15:40Z-23:35:40Z.
The new ad pod's CPU usage was 0.0393-0.0495 cores per second from 23:36:40Z to 23:43:40Z (its limit is 50m = 0.05 cores), versus 0.0041-0.0108 cores for the previous ad pod before the restart.

Deployment otel-demo/ad scaled replica set ad-785b4464f5 up from 0 to 1 at 23:35:00Z and scaled ad-554b849958 down from 1 to 0 at 23:35:02Z, with pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 23:35:00-23:35:02Z and pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc Killing at 23:35:02Z.

The new ad ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 carries the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:35:00Z, and its container spec (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, name ad, port 8080, no command/args/volumeMounts) is otherwise identical to ReplicaSet ad-554b849958; both share identical env vars (FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, AD_PORT=8080) and identical resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi).

Deployment otel-demo/ad is configured with limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi; for comparison other otel-demo deployments set limits between 5m (image-provider, quote, shipping) and 500m (load-generator).
ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) sets the fault-injection flag adFailure with description 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'on' (variants on=true, off=false).

The other fault-injection flags in the same demo.flagd.json are off: adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure all have defaultVariant 'off'.

ad's own server spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carried only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET over 23:18:40Z-23:52:40Z; no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series existed for that ad operation, and the export count dropped from 305.56 per 5m at 23:35:40Z to 0 at 23:41:40Z-23:43:40Z before recovering to 82.98 at 23:44:40Z.

Before the 23:35:00Z rollout, every ad GetAds span was within the 5,000 ms bucket (increase[5m] at le=5000.0 equalled le=+Inf from 23:18:40Z to 23:35:40Z), so the later multi-second ad spans are a change from the sampled baseline rather than a pre-existing condition in that window.
Error spans at 23:42:00Z (5m increase) were present only for frontend (973.33) and frontend-proxy (488.89); ad, recommendation, fraud-detection, payment and accounting each read 0 in that window.

Pod states at query time: ad-785b4464f5-9bshh Running and ready with 0 restarts (started 23:35:00Z); frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl and frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw Running with 0 restarts (started 23:02:54Z/23:02:56Z); flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr Running with 0 restarts (started 23:04:46Z); fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 has restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled and exit code 137, its container re-Created at 23:41:50Z.
All five nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False.

frontend-proxy's sampled error spans in the incident include 504 responses with 15.000 s duration (e.g. trace d4057d2e24ea083d01006c39cd8fcd6a at 23:42:21Z) and 503 responses with 0.56 s and 1.02 s duration at 23:44:28Z and 23:47:02Z.

The fault-injecting setting that is switched on and names the affected service - ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config flag adFailure='on' ('Fail ad service') - is the object where the fault originates; the ad Deployment rollout restart at 23:35:00Z with an unchanged pod template and the frontend-proxy 5xx errors are its mechanism and consequences, since no other object was seen applying a fault to the ad workload.

A second candidate mechanism that the evidence does not rule out: the new ad pod was cold-started under the 50m CPU limit of Deployment otel-demo/ad, was throttled 95-99.9% of CFS periods from 23:35:40Z, and therefore could not serve GetAds or complete flagd ResolveBoolean calls in time, which by itself explains the 504/500 errors independently of any flag value.

ad's own server spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no ad-side ERROR series during the spike, so the declared 'Fail ad service' behaviour itself was not observed; the observed ad failure mode was slowness and connection refusal.

The alert reports it has been firing since 23:33:40Z, but frontend-proxy and frontend error series only stepped up at 23:35:40Z-23:36:40Z, after the ad rollout restart; only 1.1-4.4 error spans per 5m existed from 23:17:40Z, so the alert's own firing timestamp is not fully explained by the observed error series.

frontend-proxy itself as the faulting component is rejected: its 504/503 responses have matching egress spans with http.status_code 0 and 15 s duration toward frontend, the pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl is Running with 0 restarts since 23:02:54Z, and the slowness is carried by frontend's /api/data and ad GetAds spans.

flagd server degradation is rejected as the primary bottleneck: flagd's own ResolveBoolean server spans completed in 49-110 microseconds and one in 9 microseconds, and the pod flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr is Running with 0 restarts; ad's multi-second client spans show the delay before flagd received each call.

fraud-detection's OOMKilled container (exit 137, container re-created 23:41:50Z) is not this cause: it is a different workload on the checkout path, its error-span count read 0 at 23:42:00Z, and no evidence links it to the frontend->ad latency or to frontend-proxy's 5xx.

Check the cluster audit/change record for who issued the rollout restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:35:00Z on Deployment otel-demo/ad, and for any edit that set adFailure to 'on' in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, before treating either as confirmed intent.

Review Deployment otel-demo/ad's 50m CPU limit and its readiness-probe timing: a fresh pod of this service needed more CPU than the limit allowed for about eight minutes, so raising the limit (or adding startup CPU headroom / a startup probe) would avoid repeating the outage on every rollout.

gaps: The alert's own metric and expression could not be verified: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules (no_data), so the annotation value 2.4555 and the firing time 23:33:40Z cannot be tied to a specific series; the observed error step-up is at 23:35:40Z-23:36:40Z, while low-level errors existed from 23:17:40Z.

The change_history integration is not available in this run, so I cannot determine when adFailure was switched to 'on' in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, nor who or what applied the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:35:00Z rollout restart to Deployment otel-demo/ad.

The declared fault was not observed directly: ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no ad-side ERROR series; only slowness and connection refusal were seen, so the link from adFailure='on' to those symptoms is unproven.

Ad pod readiness/endpoint state during 23:35-23:47 is unknown: kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned no series in this Prometheus, and no readiness-failure events were returned for pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh; the removal of ad from Service endpoints at 23:42:13Z is inferred from the ECONNREFUSED text, not observed.

Other candidate metric sources were absent: rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name='flagd' returned no series, so flagd's own error rate/latency cannot be quantified from metrics.
Frontend container logs for 23:30:00Z-23:50:00Z returned no lines (bytes_read 0), so application-log confirmation of the frontend-side errors is missing.

Services other than frontend, frontend-proxy, ad, recommendation, fraud-detection, payment and accounting were not present in the error-span query, so cart, checkout, currency, email, shipping, quote, product-catalog, image-provider, kafka, valkey-cart and the load-generator backend are unchecked for error spans, not shown healthy.

data-recorders namespace events (2 Pod FailedScheduling, 1 PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete, PVC provisioning churn) fall in the event window; I did not investigate them and found no evidence tying them to this alert.
next_steps: Retrieve the alert rule definition for RequestErrorRate (its PromQL and hold time) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files, since it is not loaded in the queried Prometheus.
Have a human reconcile the 23:35:00Z rollout restart of Deployment otel-demo/ad and the adFailure='on' entry in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config with the authorized change/chaos schedule.

Inspect the ad pod's Kubernetes readiness-probe history and Service endpoints at 23:35-23:47 with kubectl/audit tooling that retains historical state, to confirm whether ad was removed from the frontend-to-ad path.
If recurrence matters, capture ad container CPU throttling and startup timings for future rollouts as a standing check for Deployment otel-demo/ad.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
